title: Adverbs of Frequency
summary: Say how often things happen with sempre, geralmente, às vezes, raramente, and nunca.

sections.heading: Core frequency adverbs
sections.body:
Frequency adverbs describe how often an action happens. They usually appear before or after the main verb phrase, depending on emphasis.

| Portuguese | English |
|---|---|
| sempre | always |
| geralmente / normalmente | usually |
| muitas vezes | often |
| às vezes | sometimes |
| raramente | rarely |
| nunca | never |

examples.pt: Eu sempre tomo café de manhã.
examples.en: I always drink coffee in the morning.

examples.pt: A gente às vezes almoça fora.

sections.heading: Nunca and negative meaning
sections.body: **Nunca** already has negative meaning. It can appear before the verb or after a verb with **não**. In everyday sentences, **nunca** before the verb is very common.

examples.en: I have never been to Manaus.

sections.heading: Precise frequency expressions
sections.body: Use expressions with **por**, **vez(es)**, and time periods to be more precise. In Brazil, **uma vez por semana** and **duas vezes por mês** are standard patterns.

examples.pt: Faço exercício três vezes por semana.
examples.en: I exercise three times a week.

examples.pt: Visito meus pais uma vez por mês.
examples.en: I visit my parents once a month.
We have a meeting every day.

keyPoints: Sempre, geralmente, às vezes, raramente, and nunca are core frequency adverbs.
Use vezes por semana/mês/ano for exact frequency.
Todo dia means every day; todos os dias is also common.
Adverb position is flexible, but before the main verb is a safe default.

commonMistakes.note: Do not use não before nunca in the standard pre-verbal pattern.
For frequency, por semana is the standard expression.
Subject + adverb + verb is the neutral order.
